title: UK labour market overview — earnings, unemployment and vacancies (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the quarter-aligned print that SETTLES the 2026 Q4 private-wage figure the 2027-02-04 Monetary Policy Report states twelve days earlier
source: EST: two UK-government primaries fetched direct 2026-09-10 by this event's own lane, both HTTP 200, rather than inherited from the proposal. (1) gov.uk/government/statistics/announcements/uk-labour-market-february-2027 — the statutory pre-announcement register reads 'UK Labour Market February 2027', 'Release date: 16 February 2027 7:00am (confirmed)', producer Office for National Statistics, designation 'Accredited official statistics', 'Published: 2 July 2026', 'Last updated: 2 July 2026', contents 'Estimates of employment, unemployment, inactivity, average weekly earnings, vacancies and other labour market related statistics for the UK' — AND an amendment note no prior document in this chain records, verbatim: 'The release date has been changed', 'Previous date: 16 February 2026 7:00am', 'Reason for change: Input error corrected'. The three neighbouring announcements were fetched the same day for exactly that contrast and all read 'Published: 30 June 2026 / Last updated: 30 June 2026' with NO amendment note (March 2027 '16 March 2027 7:00am (confirmed)', April 2027 '20 April 2027 7:00am (confirmed)', May 2027 '18 May 2027 7:00am (confirmed)'), so the amendment is specific to this entry rather than a bulk republish of the 2027 run. (2) ons.gov.uk/releases/uklabourmarketfebruary2027 — the ONS release-calendar entry reads 'Release date: 16 February 2027 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', accredited official statistics, and carries NO provisional label, unlike its D+1 neighbour uk-cpi-2027-02-17 which ONS itself marks 'Provisional release date'. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts carries BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS:/FED: and has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap all five 2026-27 siblings were filed under. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-10 by its own lane (docs/research/events/uk-labour-market-2027-02-16.md), which read the single proposal in full — proposals/uk-labour-market-2027-02-16.from-uk-labour-market-2027-01-19.json, now inert and left in place — and re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting it. THE TITLE IS SHARPENED, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE FINDING. The proposal's title reads 'the first labour print AFTER the February forecast round rather than before it', which is accurate and treats post-round placement as the ABSENCE of the property the chain prized. This lane finds it is the STRONGER property. (1) THE CHAIN'S MISSING 2026 Q4 WAGE PATH IS THE MPR CHART'S PUBLISHED HORIZON, NOT MISSING DATA. Four sibling ledgers (10-20, 11-17, 12-15, 01-19) log 'no 2026 Q4 private-sector AWE path is published anywhere' as a fetched negative, and the 10-20 lane recorded the July 2026 MPR PDF as subset-font encoded, after which every later lane relayed the path at second hand. The Report is served as HTML at bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy-report/2026/july-2026 (HTTP 200, 7,779,563 bytes, fetched today) and reads cleanly: 'Annual private sector AWE growth is projected to average 2.8% in 2026 Q2 and around 3.0% in Q3 (Chart 1.4, gold diamonds)', with the footnote 'The private sector regular pay growth projection diamonds are for the three months to June and September 2026' — the Bank stating one path in both notations, direct evidence the two name the same object. Across three consecutive Reports fetched today the diamonds never pass the CURRENT quarter: Feb 2026 'quarterly projections for 2025 Q4-2026 Q2', Apr 2026 'projection diamonds are for 2026 Q1 and 2026 Q2' (text '3.1% in 2026 Q1 before falling slightly to 3.0% in 2026 Q2'), Jul 2026 Q2/Q3. So NO published Report could have carried a Q4-2026 diamond; the first whose horizon reaches it is the November 2026 one, listed CONFIRMED on the Bank's own page as 'November MPC Summary and minutes and November Monetary Policy Report', dated 2026-11-05, 103 days before this print. Rule banked: a negative result deserves the same scrutiny as a positive one. (2) THIS WINDOW IS EXACTLY A CALENDAR QUARTER, AND ONLY ONE RELEASE IN FOUR IS. The window rule was reconfirmed firsthand for the FIFTH time from the 18 August 2026 bulletin (Apr-Jun 2026 AWE/LFS, May-Jul vacancies 707,000, July payroll flash 30.3m, 'Next release: 15 September 2026'): a release in month M carries months M-4 to M-2, which equals a calendar quarter only for the FEBRUARY, MAY, AUGUST and NOVEMBER releases. So this print's Oct-Dec 2026 window IS 2026 Q4 and an MPR quarterly diamond maps onto it 1:1 with no blending — which no sibling window allowed, and which is exactly why none of them could set an absolute threshold honestly. The 2026-11-17 sibling is also quarter-aligned (Jul-Sep = Q3) and never noted the alignment. (3) POST-ROUND PLACEMENT IS THE STRONGER PROPERTY AND THE CHAIN HAD IT BACKWARDS. bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates, fetched today under the literal header '2027 provisional dates', lists Thursday 4 February as 'February MPC Summary and minutes and February Monetary Policy Report' and Thursday 18 March as 'March MPC Summary and minutes' (current Bank Rate 3.75%). This print is D+12 after the February Report, D-30 before the March round, and the next labour print (2027-03-16) is both the D-2 read before that round AND the first wholly post-Budget window — so this print has neither property the chain prized. Inverted: by (1) the February 2027 Report's just-ended-quarter diamond is 2026 Q4, whose AWE is STILL UNPUBLISHED on 2027-02-04 (the 2027-01-19 release carries Sep-Nov), and by (2) this window is that quarter exactly. The Report therefore states a Q4 figure twelve days before ONS prints the actual one, on the same window, with no blending — the tightest forecast-vs-outcome pairing in the six-entry chain. A pre-round print can be INCORPORATED; a post-round print can be SCORED. (4) THE MECHANISM'S ONLY CLEAN PRECEDENT IS DISQUALIFIED ON THIS LANE'S OWN ARGUMENT: the July MPR projected 2.8% for Q2 and the 18 August bulletin printed private regular pay 2.8% for Apr-Jun, same quarter and same decimal — but the Report published 2026-07-30 with the three months to May already at 2.9%, i.e. two of three months in hand, so the diamond was a NOWCAST. The honest instance is the Q3 diamond (zero AWE months published at Report time), printing 2026-11-17, 91 days before this event. THE BUDGET QUESTION IS NOT REOPENED: the 01-19 lane settled that the first wholly post-Budget AWE window is Nov 2026-Jan 2027, published 2027-03-16, and this event's own proposal already carries that correction. Restated only in the sibling's own convention (days strictly after Budget day 2026-10-28, which is how it reached 33 of 91): this window is 64 of 92 days post-Budget, against 3 of 92 for Aug-Oct and 33 of 91 for Sep-Nov. TWO DATED ADJACENCIES PROPOSED, both register-fetched today and both load-bearing for finding (2): uk-labour-market-2027-05-18, the next quarter-aligned release (Jan-Mar 2027 = 2027 Q1, the next instance of this lane's own scoring mechanism), and uk-labour-market-2027-04-20, D-9 before the already-tracked boe-decision-2027-04-29 April Report round. MINOR SIBLING CORRECTION, recorded not edited: the 01-19 lane called boe-decision-2027-02-04 and boe-decision-2027-03-18 a 'real calendar gap' with neither present; both already existed as proposals from the UK CPI chain (from-uk-cpi-2027-01-20, from-uk-cpi-2027-04-21) — the gap was in CANONICAL files only. IMPACT LOW, argued not inherited: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol, no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed, and the measured cable reaction to the 2026-08-18 release was ~0.1% on a two-sided beat. THE CORRIDOR IS THE THINNEST OF THE SIX AND ONE OF ITS IDS IS A PHANTOM: 9 tracked ids within five days (vs 13 for 01-19 and 35 for 12-15) but only 8 distinct real-world events — presidents-day-market-closure-2027-02-15 and washingtons-birthday-market-closure-2027-02-15 are the same NYSE row, tracked as issue #1609, so this event's adjacentIds double-counts one holiday. D-1 is a US closure for the SECOND consecutive print in this chain (markets shut Monday 02-15, UK open), so the print lands in the pre-open of the first US session after a three-day weekend exactly as 01-19 did behind MLK — two for two, and US-open attribution is worse than the thin count implies both times. No Fed blackout is running (fomc-2027-01-27 at D-20, fomc-minutes-2027-02-17 at D+1), a regression from the 01-19 print's one improvement over its sibling. The UK data runs two days again with this print first (uk-cpi-2027-02-17, canonical, estimate) — but per that lane's own finding the CPI print is the first of two annual weight updates, so a 02-17 sterling move has a weights-methodology explanation before a labour one. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
